column1: # The qdot-rate floor table, the one owner of the pairs tools/ref/qdot-rate.sh rules: a Rust qdot-rate row
# (type, k) and the ik harness that times the same type at the same row bytes; the floor is the lowest
# same-round ratio ours/ik a sitting may read (tools/ref/qdot-rate-floors.py check: one round under it
# ends the runner rc 1, naming the row). The runner runs the harnesses this table names, in its order.
# Derivation of the derived rows (tools/ref/qdot-rate-floors.py derive, its docstring's rule): the six
# rounds of two A6000-box sittings, one pinned core, pooled — 2026-10-07T16:39Z (worker1 m2rate, three
# rounds) and 2026-10-09T23:59Z (glmiq4 s2-rate, three rounds; the IQ3_S row only there). Per row:
# floor = mean - t(1 - 0.05/60, 5) * sd * sqrt(1 + 1/6) - res * mean, t = 6.138 (10 rows x 6 rounds
# = 60 checks a sitting at most), res = the two times' print resolution; written rounded down to 0.01.
# The kernels these rows time are the same functions in the -sse4a build (tools/ref/asm-census.py diff
# of the two qdot-rate builds: only dot_iq3s_q8k_avx2 and the scalar mirrors' dot_row_scalar_ty moved),
# so the base sittings rule it. The pooling holds because the two sittings' one-column rows read the same
# within their SD (their trees may differ by dae925ca, the multi-column tiles, which these rows do not run).
# PIN(2026-10-10): 0.9, set by the iq3sfix spec, not derived: the base sitting read 0.133-0.135 (two
# extrq in the AVX loop, docs/cards/iq3sfix-rate.card); the -sse4a build was predicted at ~~1.15-1.20~~
# and read 0.975 / 0.961 / 0.979 in the quiet sitting of 2026-10-10T06:41Z (its loop runs at 0.81x the
# IQ3_XXS loop's IPC, not 1x), so 0.9 sits 0.06 under that sitting's lowest round and is red on the base
